utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic is continuing his questions. Your affirmation to tell the truth continues to apply.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I've discovered how we can prevent ourselves from speaking too quickly and allowing the interpreters to do their work, maybe we should take a deep breath before we start with either question or an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a document D004-1611.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, are you familiar with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It was sent by the staff to all the SUPs in Kosovo. We can see the contents here, but I would like to know in the given period, so this was on the 11th of November, 1998, here we can see that the activity of the KLA had increased. Do you know in the territory of your SUP, for example, whether they took any positions, whether they retook any positions wherefrom they withdrew during the summer of 1998, so the positions that were then controlled by the authorities of Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the completion of anti-terrorist activities at the end of September 1998, the control was regained over the entire territory of Kosovo and Metohija. I'm talking about the control by the police and the army. After the signing of the Holbrooke-Milosevic Agreement and after the arrival of the OSCE Mission to Kosovo and Metohija, one part of the police forces were withdrawn from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. In that that period from October onwards, that is in November and December, all the positions that were previously controlled by the police station and the Army of Yugoslavia were slowly taken by the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the attacks by KLA to roads, police forces, the army, also initiate various other incidents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Until the end of 1998, they weren't that frequent; but after the beginning of 1999, they became more frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, to you know that members of the KLA were also active when wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know during this entire period, 1998 and 1999, that when their forces were crushed, that they would mingle with the civilian population wearing civilian clothes in order to prevent being detained?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of them wore military uniforms, and on top of them they wore civilian clothes. And the other way around, they would have a military uniform and underneath they would wear civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is capturing and arresting terrorist and their prosecution by the police part of a regular police activity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of the public services and state services, primarily of the state services.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any criminal reports filed by the SUP Kosovska Mitrovica against terrorists to the relevant courts?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And is this a part of the permanent activities of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Having received information that somebody participated in terrorist activities, that there were attacks against members of the army, police, Serbian population, or Serbian refugees in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, or against loyal Albanians; so immediately after we received that information, SUP would undertake all the relevant measures and start -- initiate procedures against such persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica throughout 1998 and 1999 carried out its regular police duties?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's regular police duties in line with the law and regulations on the internal organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D246, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the document under 65 ter list 04165. 4156? This is not the right document. Under 65 ter list 04165.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, are you familiar with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I have several questions regarding this dispatch. Here we can see that it's been established that the KLA was -- that the Kosovo Verification Mission had certain implications towards the Albanian terrorists, so are you familiar with the activities of the monitoring mission in terms of the fact that they were monitoring and taking pictures of certain facilities in Kosovo that they were not supposed to do, bridges, certain roads, certain facilities, and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know anything specific concerning this. There were some rumours about their inclination, but I really do not know anything specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any problem in the territory of your SUP in relation to the members of the Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, there were two missions in the territory of Kosovo. The OSCE Mission and the diplomatic Verification Mission, so I would once again like to point out that we had excellent cooperation with the diplomatic Verification Mission because we carried out certain activities together very successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D247, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have D004-1935.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is, again, a dispatch sent from the staff to all the SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija ordering, as we can see, to undertake certain measures pursuant to the law. I would like to know what is it that you did in the area of SUP Kosovska Mitrovica having received this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certain measures were undertaken against person who perpetrated certain criminal offences, and approximately 100 criminal reports were filed with SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica by April the 16th, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It will be marked for identification, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D248 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. It seems to me that we should have, if fact, a translation of this document, but that's quite okay. We can find it later on. Can I please have the document D004-1827.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is the dispatch by -- sent by the staff on 2nd of April to chiefs of all the SUPs in Kosovo. Could you please read it for yourself in order to familiarise yourself with the content, and then tell me what was it that you did specifically in the territory of SUP Kosovska Mitrovica in relation to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This dispatch was submitted to the chiefs of SUPs, PJP commanders, and we held meetings with members of the Yugoslav Army. We sent up joint check-points that were manned by police and army, and we carried out the tasks as described in the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is why we received these approximately 100 criminal reports that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D249 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, concerning all the crimes you were informed about, did you undertake all of the measures prescribed by the law in Kosovska Mitrovica SUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took measures or acted upon all information we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the second half of 1998 and in 1999, is it true that for the most part Albanians stopped reporting crime and that to a great extent this made the work of the SUPs in Kosovo-Metohija that much harder in terms of detecting and apprehending the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in Kosovo-Metohija in late 1996 pursuant to an order in early 1997, it is unknown to me that they ever reported to the SUP the commission of any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not change throughout the time I was there. And even if there were reports, these were sporadic or individual cases because I simply cannot recall any such particular events and I cannot provide you with any examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have Defence Exhibit 004-1829.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is an Official Note drafted at the MUP staff on the 5th of April. I am not sure whether you are familiar with it and whether the information contained therein was ever conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you specifically what information I received and by what means and what way. On the 5th of April, in the afternoon, I received a phone call from General Lukic who was in charge of the staff. On that occasion, he told me the following: Immediately prevent the departure of civilians outside their places of residence. That was number one. Number two, those already on the move should be returned to their residence. Thirdly, secure an appropriate number of buses for that purpose and return all civilians along the roads to their homes. Fourthly, all civilians should be guaranteed safety in the location where they live and in their movements about. Fifthly, all those attacking civilians should be punished harshly. Acquaint all PJP commanders with this order as well as all military commanders. Fighting terrorism remains our priority task. This order should not be discussed with other persons. In brief, this is what was conveyed to me on the 5th of April over the phone. That was in the afternoon. What did I do as the chief of the Secretariat? At 6.00 p.m. the same day, I summoned all PJP commanders, as well as all military commanders in that area. But in the area of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, there was only the deputy commander of the 125th Motorised Brigade. As well as the commander of the military territorial detachment or organ. They were then asked to acquaint their respective commanders with the contents of the order. The commander of the 35th and 75th PJP Detachments were also acquainted with the contents of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document MFI'd since the translation is pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D250 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document D004-1677 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we are about to see a dispatch of the 16th of March by the chief of the public security sector sent to all SUPs and the staff as well as all the addressees. Could you please have a look at it to acquaint yourself with the document. Do you remember this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. It was discussed at a meeting in the staff when the minister said that Serbs should not believe certain misinformation and propaganda, and in essence, that they should not leave Kosovo since some of them had apartments in other parts of the Republic of Serbia and they simply wanted to change their places of residence. Some did so in order to avoid certain of their obligations in terms of tax, some did so for personal reasons, whereas others had some reasons of their own. And, sorry, let me just add something. The Secretariats were prohibited from allowing these people to change their place of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D251, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have D004-1819.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, have a look at the stamp in the English version because there we can see the date, whereas in the Serbian we can hardly make it out.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 22nd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, was this dispatch sent to all SUPs in the territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It has to do with the dispatch number 312 of the 18th of February, which was created pursuant to the conclusions following a meeting at the staff held on the 17th of February. Everything that the minister said on that occasion was translated into the tasks contained in Dispatch 312, and this dispatch is a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this a period of immediate threat of war during which NATO attacks were expected?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such a possibility was seriously contemplated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the state was undertaking different measures to defend itself against the aggression?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in keeping with the plans drafted at the federal level, we were supposed to undertake certain measures and procedures to defend the sovereignty and territorial integrity as well as independence of the constitutional order and state.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any differences between the SUPs in Kosovo and others in terms of implementing this order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no difference. All Secretariats had to implement the tasks of Dispatch 312. Not only the Secretariats of the Interior, but also the centres of the public security sector and their organisational units by which I mean their departments since they all received the same dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 16, page 10, should read the "state" security sector. We can also have the witness repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, the dispatch you mentioned, Dispatch 312, who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the sector -- to the public security sector and all administrations within that sector as well as to the organisational units within the sector of public security. And to the sector of state security as well as its organisational units within their respective services. Those organisational units within the state security service were the centres of the sector. Their subordinate organisational units were the departments of the public -- state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It was sent to them for information?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also to undertake certain measures. So for information and to undertake those measures which fall within their remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D252, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1685 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we'll see another dispatch of the 27th of March by the head of sector sent to all SUPs, to the staff, to border police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I'm unable to read the contents on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: First of all, it was sent to all the SUPs in the territory Serbia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you do anything specifically following this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rumour had it at the time that once the OSCE Mission withdrew from Kosovo that they left behind certain locators used for guiding NATO aeroplanes. In this dispatch, it is stated that such locators are also dropped from aeroplanes in certain areas as to use them for NATO aeroplane guidance. In the territory of our SUP, I had no knowledge of such devices in the territory. In certain parts of the territory of Kosovo, there may have been some though.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked. We now have a translation on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You do? Excellent. Then I seek to tender it. I no longer saw the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be an exhibit now with that number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D253, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have document 5316 on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is another dispatch of the head of the public security sector of the 12th of April, 1999, sent to all chiefs of SUPs. Could you please have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please have a hard copy since I'm unable to read anything on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I underlined certain interesting portions of the document. Do you want me to read it out for you? Perhaps I can jog your memory. That is the 12th of April, 1999, to all chiefs of SUP from 1 to 33 and to the chiefs of administrations: In the conditions of the state of war and daily NATO bombardment that our country has been exposed to, it is necessary to undertake the following measures: 1, in cooperation with the town and municipality civilian protection staffs, organise members of hunting and marksmen scouting, mountaineering, and other organisations; to monitor, inform and search the terrain in order to find bombing markers. Number 2, with district chiefs, examine the problem of supply and demand of legal entities, natural persons for oil and its derivatives seize artificial fertilizers, et cetera. Vigorously prevent all forms of speculative behaviour. Maintain contact with permanent judicial and other government organs. Do you recall this Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this dispatch. Concerning this cooperation, it was in place in terms of cooperation with civilian protection and the monitoring and alarming service. In keeping with defence plans, both services in the state of war had their tasks. However, I do not remember this specific dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have D004-2899.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may have been forwarded to my deputy or the chief of the OKP or the chief of police, but I really cannot remember it at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no problem with that, although I think your memory is excellent. D004-2899, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram of the public security sector head after you left Mitrovica. I just want you to have a look at the format and his signature.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can just see the signature, please. Yes, this is the signature of the assistant minister chief of the public security sector and this was the usual form of dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D254, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly see the document 004-1692.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a telegram sent by the head of crime police administration to all the SUPs in the territory of Serbia, dated 26th of March, 1999, so I wonder whether you recall receiving this telegram?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in. Yes, I did receive this dispatch. I'm familiar with it, and the department for the suppression of crime in the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica acted according to this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we kindly tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D255, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have a document under 65 ter 04023.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is yet another document of the crime police administration dated April the 6th, sent to chiefs of all the SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija. Could you please take a look at it and tell us whether it corresponds to the form that you can recognise and what was it that you did pursuant to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, you suggested this was sent. It appears to be notes of a briefing session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that the number, I do not -- is not in line, so I asked for a document under 65 ter list 04023 and this is not the document I was looking for. Possibly it was my mistake so let us proceed in order not to waste any time. Madam O'Leary, I'm sure we'll find the right document later on. So can I please have the document D004-1694. Could we kindly see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a telegram sent by the crime police administration to the MUP staff and SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija on 11th of April, 1999. Did you receive this dispatch? Is the form the one corresponding to your recollection, and what was it that you did pursuant to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The form is all right, but it wasn't only sent to the MUP staff and the Secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija, but also the Secretariats in the region bordering with Kosovo and Metohija. Why to them? Well, because these Secretariats had certain check-points where they controlled the goods entering and exiting the territory of Kosevo and Metohija. They were registering these goods in order to try and prevent any smuggling, so this is what this dispatch was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D256, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So the document I was actually looking for under 65 ter list was the document 42023. Actually, the numbers were replaced in order but this is the same document, the document of the crime police administration from Belgrade dated 6th of April. So 65 ter 4203, whereas I put the wrong number on the list, I put on the list the number 4023 and instead it should have been 4203. So I would kindly ask Mr. Stamp to tell me whether he agrees that I can use this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No objections to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stamp. I hope it is all right with Your Honours as well for me to use this document. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, so this is the document on 65 ter list 04203. Mr. Cvetic, do you recognise the format of this document? Once again, it was sent, as I can see, to the SUPs in the entire territory of Serbia. If you received it, what was it that you did following the reception of this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the format of the dispatch that was used, and with this dispatch the Secretariats of the Interior were informed that the government of the Republic of Serbia adopted a decree amending certain parts of The Criminal Code and that this decree was published in the Official Gazette. Here we can see the number of the Official Gazette. And that this came into effect on April the 5th. What was the goal of this dispatch? It was to underline the application of the Criminal Procedures Act so the Criminal Procedures Act that was in effect, so to call, peacetime Criminal Procedures Act; and if there was a reason then Criminal Procedures Act that was to be applied in times of war was to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 257, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the document D004-1763.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a document sent by the chief --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Spasic, yes, I know him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It was sent on the 22nd of March, have you received this or did you receive this and it is a recognisable format?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is recognisable. I am aware of this dispatch, and the territorial fire prevention unit in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica acted upon this particular order or actually it was our fire prevention section which also included a fire prevention police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D258, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see D004-1699.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a dispatch of the public security sector dated 9th of April, 1999, sent to all the SUPs in the territory of Serbia sent by Mr. Stojan Misic, assistant minister. So I would like to know whether you can recognise this form, whether you received this dispatch, whether you are familiar with its contents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this form is quite all right. It wasn't only sent to chief of Secretariats, but also to border police stations, that is, the commanders of the border police stations; and the person in charge of the bored police station at the level of the ministry was Mr. Stojan Misic. And, yes, we were informed again that the government of Yugoslavia adopted a decree whereby any travelling abroad was banned for military conscripts, and we were all obliged to act in accordance with this decree, and this is something that is very logical for the state of war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit D259, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the document D004-1711. And if we can immediately see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a dispatch, an instruction issued by the Federal Customs Administration. Can you recall this dispatch that was sent by the border police administration?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent to the Secretariat just for information, and it was also sent to the border police stations in order for them to undertake certain measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This format is the one you can recall?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D260, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see the document under 65 ter list 04285.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a dispatch sent by the assistant minister General Stojan Misic on April 19th, 1999, to all the SUPs in the territory of Serbia. First of all, I would like to know whether you can recognise the form of the document, and also given the date, whether you are familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The form is all right, but anything that received -- that was received by the SUP Kosovska Mitrovica after April the 16th was not of my interest anymore for the reasons that you are aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D261, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I see a document under 65 ter list 04166.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I would just like to know whether you can recognise the form of this document because it is dated April the 21st. It is a dispatch by the assistant minister General Zekovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 2 for the Chamber to be able to see what the document is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D262, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask for Defence document number 004-1753. Can we please see the second page because I believe you were able to see the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with this, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is a signed dispatch, the chief of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You forwarded this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: With the instructions attached?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D263, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, the document that was just admitted is your dispatch forwarding the dispatch you received from the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-0021 next.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counsel, please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. D004 -- sorry, 04-0021. It is probably my mistake. Let us move on. I would next ask for 004-1833.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a plan to prevent any disturbances of public order and law. On the first page it says: Official Secret, Kolubara.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this is July 1997?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The stamp says -- or rather, the header says that it's the 30th of July, 1997?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kolubara plans existed prior to my arrival in the area of Kosovo and Metohija. They had been put together during a certain period of time by certain representatives of the army and the police to the extent of my knowledge. The goal of those documents was as follows: If there are disturbances of public order and law on a large scale and if there are any inter-ethnic conflicts, certain measures that need to be undertaken by all organs in Kosovo were supposed to be dealt with. That is in gist the contents. The plan had its textural parts, a number of tables, and sketches or schematics. It was all worked out in detail, who was to do what, when, where, and with whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I'm not mistaken, and I'll try to remind you, the president of the FRY at the time of adoption of this document was Zoran Lilic. He, as the president of the republic -- or rather, this document was adopted by the Supreme Defence Council at the federal level?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D264 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter document number 4116. This is page 1. Could we please have page 2 displayed. Page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is your document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my document in which I forwarded the document from the ministry to the head of aliens department to acquaint himself with the contents and undertake measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We don't have that document on the screen. We have a document of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the first page is the document signed by the witness and this is an attachment forwarded or rather drafted by my client. The witness simply sent that document to his head of aliens department. Could we please go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D265, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1843.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you recognise this type of document? Did you see it while you were in the territory?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certain plans were drafted but this term, the plan of defence of the city of Vucitrn, I'm not sure it's quite adequate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to the second page. The third page, please. Page 4, please. Page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There. Under 3, you see?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said at the beginning, the term, the plan of defence of the city. Defence is a very comprehensive terms encompassing many different parts of the defence system, whereas this only concerned one segment, the security segment in a single area exclusively to have any terrorist incursions prevented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to that later, but at the meeting of the staff on the 28th of July, did General Lukic address such plans?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I was being questioned by Mr. Prosecutor, I said that these were defensive plans, or rather, plans of protection of personnel and facilities. And which forces were to be used to provide that security to secure the facilities, people, and roads. So as to establish such a security situation in the territory that could be sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Given the period, why was this topical? What was the security situation like?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, it was complex. Yesterday I only pointed out one part of that complex situation in the area of Drenica in Srbica to be more precise. I pointed out the example of a single road, but many roads were unsafe to use in the area. In the area of Vucitrn, all mountains at the foot of Mount Cicavica, all the villages from Zilivoda to Pantina, so there is between 10 and 15 villages there, were in danger. Those villages needed protection because the Serb population raised the issue of not taking any measures for their safety. That's why such defence and protection plans were drawn. These were protection plans since they were defensive in nature. They were not offensive plans envisaging any attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A parallel just comes to mind. It is the obligation of the SUPs to protect certain facilities even in times of peace?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This falls within the remit of keeping law and order and the functioning of the system of governance and all organs and organisations in the territory of the individual SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D266 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvetic -- sorry, I would ask for D004-1765.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is your dispatch. Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next have D004-1855.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a response of the Zubin Potok police station to your previous dispatch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we have a translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't. We don't? Then could we please have it marked for identification. I probably mixed it up with the previous one. Could we please have it MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You said -- this is the 30th of August. This is the 30th of June, you said it was a response to a dispatch in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I misspoke. A minute ago we admitted the dispatch of the witness sent on the 30th of June to the departments and police stations. What I'm asking to be MFI'd is the response following his dispatch of the same date sent to the witness, to the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, concerning the issues referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are not content. We need to see the previous dispatch, which is Exhibit D267.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the heading of the document that you can see right now, the date is 30th of June, and there is a dispatch number there, 269, in the top left corner. If we could just see the previous document on the screen. All right. That is the one. In the top-left corner, the mistake is the following: It is supposed to be 30th of June and we see that there is an error in the translation in the English language. It says 30th of August. It's supposed to be June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well, the response of the 30th of June will be marked, because there's no translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D268 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, and only after this, what followed was the document that we already received as an exhibit, and this was your response to the staff dated 1st of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can proceed. Can we please have the Defence document 004-1939.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is, once again, a dispatch sent by the staff on July the 10th, 1998. It is a brief dispatch but unfortunately we still do not have the translation. Could you please slowly read this out, this dispatch, if you can see it. Or shall I read it and you can tell me whether you agree with what I read?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please, because I can read this with great difficulty on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So this is the dispatch of the MUP staff number 12A dated 10th of July, 1998, and it says PS, Leposavic, Vucitrn, Srbica, Zubin Potok, Zvecan --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise but now I can see this better. Yes. This is a dispatch that was forwarded, and it was submitted by the ministry staff to the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica, and the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica forwarded it to all the police stations in its territory. So to the police stations Leposavic, Vucitrn, Srbica, Zubin Potok, Zvecan, and also to the police stations in its seat in Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. So you forwarded it on the 10th of July or after the 10th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is stated in the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please MFI this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D269 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the document D005-1858.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There was no interpretation of your question then -- or the answer, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, the dispatch that we saw a minute ago that was admitted into evidence dated 10th of July, 1998, was sent by the MUP staff in Pristina to you and you forwarded it on to your subordinate units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent by the MUP staff to the Secretariats or actually to the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica, and the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica forwarded it to all the police stations in its territory and also to the police station in its seat, that is in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the document D004-1858.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, are you familiar when it comes to the reserve police squads that this was what a plan for a reserve police squad looked like, this is one I found, this is for the reserve police squad in Zubce.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we kindly see the second page. Can we see the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, is this a defence plan? Is that the point of this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a plan of engagement of the reserve police squad in case that there was an attack against an inhabited area. This particular plan was developed by the police station Zubin Potok since the village of Zubce belongs to the municipality of Zubin Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here we can see that in the village the population of the village is 542 and the plan envisages 22 members of the reserve police squad to be issued infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to the second page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You can see down there the plan of personnel and materiel establishment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just add, in order to a have a complete answer, for the defence of a village apart from the engagement of this police reserve squad with 22 members, there were also other members which, according to the wartime establishment, were put into other structures of defence. So the number would have been higher if there was an attack, or actually, if certain measures were to be undertaken to defend the village in peacetime. In wartime, however, the members of the reserve police squad would go to their respective positions, to their respective units, according to the war plan establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this supplement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D270 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appears a convenient time, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is time. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please see the document D004-1868.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you recall documents of this type?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the second page. Can we please see the third page. And the fourth page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, could you please comment on this document. This is the training plan?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every year, a plan of training and development was elaborated. This was an obligation of all the Secretariats in the territory of Serbia, and it was developed at the level of the Secretariat and submitted to all the organisational units of the Secretariat; and upon the implemented plan, the report on its implementation was also submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This plan was developed for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia for all of the SUPs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please mark this document for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D271 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the document D004-1719.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Should we zoom in, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we possibly zoom it just a little bit more and scroll down just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you remember this dispatch of yours?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that the minister adopted a decision on rewarding members of MUP and decided on awards for their participation in anti-terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This could only be done by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this was, in a way, implementation of his decision made by you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to a proposal of the Secretariat, at the level of the ministry all the proposals were considered, and these proposals had to be justified in detail as to why certain persons were proposed for certain award or promotion into a higher rank. And the minister and his associates most be probably at the sessions of the collegium decided which particular individuals were to be promoted or awarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D272, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, now that we are discussing this topic, the extraordinary promotion into a higher rank pursuant to the law, this was a decision of the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a possibility to have this extraordinary procedure for promotion, and this was pursuant to the Law on the Ranks which was adopted in keeping with the Law on the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember that the minister decided also to award financial awards to certain members of the police, I believe it was around September?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were awards in form of money, but also there were awards in form of pistols, for example, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's been received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Then please D004-1721.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, now, we will see a report of the police station Zubin Potok in relation to your previous dispatch. So could you please confirm that this is in fact what happened?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a response of the commander of the police station Zubin Potok sent to the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica, but to the police department, and this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D273, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the document D004-1811. Can we see the second page of this document in B/C/S. In the English language we can already see the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a daily report dated January the 14th sent by SUP Kosovska Mitrovica to the ministry staff, the leader of the ministry staff. And it was sent by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The foundation for this kind of the report, was it the act issued by the staff on the 21st of October, 1998, which we already saw in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under item 2 here, we can see regular patrol duties that were carried out on that day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on certain roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we just explain this. While they were doing this, the employees of the SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica who were also members of PJPs, they carry out these tasks as part of their regular police duties?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then we have the part of the report referring to the events which took place and then what was planned in terms of the regular police duties performance?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D274, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next have D004-1806 next. 1806.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we are about to see daily information and you as the chief of the Mitrovica SUP sent to the operation centre in Belgrade and the MUP staff in Pristina dated the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This has to do with the events of the 14th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This was done pursuant to the instruction on passing information. That was the basis of this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D275, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1894 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, you are about to see a numerical overview that was sent on the 15th to the operation centre in Belgrade and to Pristina referring to the 14th of January, 1999; is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to add, it was sent by the shift leaders of duty operations offices to the operation centre in Belgrade and to the MUP staff in Pristina. As I have said already, all that information was sent to the operations service registered in the daily log; and based on that, information sheets are then compiled and forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D276, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1800 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is another report that you sent to the ministerial staff dated the 15th of January, 1999. The basis is the same, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The previous one had do with the 14th, and this one has do with the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D277, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did counsel say that this document was sent to the ministry staff, the ministerial staff? I'm not sure if that is what is represented in the document. Maybe I didn't hear correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says to the staff of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, I can tell you that this type of reporting had to do exclusively with the staff pursuant to the dispatch forwarded to all the Secretariats in the area of Kosovo and Metohija by the staff. This type of reporting did not have anything to do with the ministry because the ministry never asked for such information from the Secretariats. It was asked for by the staff in Pristina pursuant to its dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we next have D004-1795.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is another daily report sent by the police squad of the SUP Kosovska Mitrovica to the staff and the operation centre in Belgrade on the 16th of January, 1999, referring to the events of the 15th of January, 1999; is that so, Witness?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is a different type of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We know that. We said that the first time around that the other type of reporting was pursuant to instructions and that now you say this is a different type.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous one was following the staff's request and its dispatch, and this is following the instruction on passing on information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D278, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1793.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, we will have the numerical overview for that day concerning the events and information sent to the operation centre in Belgrade and the staff in Pristina by the police department in Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I said that such matters would be forwarded by the shift leader and the duty office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D279, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1788.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a report for the 16th of January, 1999, which you sent to the staff of the ministry in Pristina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D280, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have D004-1782.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a daily report sent by the police squad to the operation centre and the staff of the ministry. The date is the 17th of January referring to the events of the 16th of January, 1999; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, you do not appear to be drawing attention to any particular event. We have had evidence of a requirement for daily reporting by each SUP and that this was complied with, and this is now the fourth of those on consecutive days that you are simply tendering. What is the purpose of this continued tendering of this type of report?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the last day [as interpreted] I wanted to tender. The purpose was to show that there were differences in the way of reporting to the MUP staff and the operation centre in Belgrade and the ministry itself. I think this is evident when looking at these reports. One can conclude what the difference in terms of reporting was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what's that going to do for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The use is in that you can see that in the regular reports it is only reported on daily events, and the staff is reported to concerning every-day activities of the previous day and as well as the activities of the next day. This is not something that the MUP was informed about in Belgrade. From this, derive the authorities of the staff. In this part in keeping with the MUP staff dispatch there was a deviation from the instructions on the passing on of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are not inclined to receive this document, Mr. Djurdjic. If there is any relevance that's going to be demonstrated, it can be from the documents we already have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. Could we please have D004 -- actually, no, in cooperation with the Prosecutor, since they have shown great understanding concerning the staff of the ministry, was informed about events and since a number of documents concerning that topic have already been admitted, the Defence proposed to the Prosecution with which the Prosecution agreed, that the daily reports of the MUP staff in Pristina that were sent to Belgrade and to the SUPs in Kosovo be admitted pursuant to the list we proposed to the Bench so as not to have to go through all of them day by day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have that list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do. I believe it was sent to the Bench. And the Prosecution is also in agreement as they confirmed in the e-mail they sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber does not have a list. If there is a list and you say that it is of a number of reports and that they are being tendered by consent, is that the proposal? They will be received and the Court Officer, when she receives the list, in due course will give appropriate exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have D004-1773.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we'll see two documents which should illustrate how a criminal procedure or proceedings were initiated. I have one of those documents pertaining to your SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the layout of such disciplinary reports that were sent?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The layout is prescribed by the instruction on disciplinary responsibility of the employees of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this document MFI'd, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D281, Your Honours, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-1768 next. Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you follow the same procedure?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, in keeping with the instructions and decree on disciplinary responsibility of the employees of the MUP, the immediate superior submits a report on the violation of work obligation against an employee of his or hers; and based on that report, the chief of the Secretariat issues a request to initiate disciplinary proceedings to the disciplinary prosecutor. The same practice was followed across all of the 33 Secretariats in Serbia as it was stipulated by the Law on Internal Affairs, and in particular by the decree on disciplinary responsibility of the employees of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D282, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have Exhibit P356.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a dispatch of the 18th of February, 1999, of the chief of the public security sector number 312. Who is the last addressee?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state security sector at headquarters to the chief for information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This means that by this dispatch, the chief was being informed on the measures undertaken by the public security sector in terms of preparations should there come an attack, a NATO attack on the territory of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the measures put forth by the minister at the meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina on the 17th of February, 1999. It was also attended by the chief of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this dispatch was sent to all of the SUPs in the territory of Serbia, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Its basis is Article 9 on the Rules of the Internal Affairs and the Law on Defence, the federal law?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one can put it that way, but it is also on the basis of an assessment of the security situation. Such a dispatch could be sent in such a case as well to point out specific security elements and measures needed to overcome such problems and to prevent any potential consequences should there be an aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next I'd like to have Exhibit P1061.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you meaning to tender this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was already admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The number, please? Thank you, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think you will be pleased to hear that we have come to the documents which have already been admitted, and the witness wanted to say something about it after Mr. Stamp's examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, now you will see a document that you were shown previously by Mr. Stamp. This is the plan of the operations of the radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly see the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember that you were shown this document by Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said you recognise this OSA and IBAR code and for the rest you said you didn't know who they were?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember, but I know about IBAR and OSA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when you were shown the second page of the document, then you could see the call-sign for the Joint Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While I was in Kosovo, I didn't hear about this call-sign. I didn't even know that this was the call-sign for the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, am I right to say that it was on the minister to decide who will be sent to Kosovo and Metohija and when?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was exclusively the right of the minister to decide on all the duties pertaining to the work of the ministry and pertaining to human resources issues. But such decisions were also made at the sessions of the collegium, and we saw previously the decision on the establishment of the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that the minister decided himself who will accompany him or go to various meetings with him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the Exhibit number -- later on, I cannot see the number, in order not to waste any time. So on the 65 ter list, 03123. But this is already an exhibit. This is the -- these are the minutes of the staff dated 28th of July, 1998. And I wanted to ask two things. Possibly if we could see page 4 in --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If counsel could clarify the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would help us if you gave the exhibit number of the documents that are already tendered, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, I will find the exhibit number now. This was the number under 65 ter list, so this is P688.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since you know what happened at the meeting on the 28th of July, there is no need to show this to you again. But bearing in mind that meeting and the statements by Minister Stojiljkovic, could you tell us what was your view of the way in which he treated and the way in which he addressed other members present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So did he provide information and instructions in all different spheres of activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and at the same time he was the vice-president of the government, and he also came to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in that capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to remind you, if I may, on page 4 in B/C/S and page 6 in English. You see here -- no, you still cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on page 6 in B/C/S, it was my error, I apologise. And in English this is on page 6 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see here -- okay, excellent. Major Radovan Vucurevic and his entire statement given at that meeting on the 28th. Can you refresh your memory concerning this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I honestly cannot remember that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but according to these minutes, he referred this information to the minister. He actually stated this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what follows from these minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 8, please. Actually, there is no need. Let us move on not to waste any time. Can we please see the document P689. Can we please see the first page, please. Or actually, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here we can see at the end that you participated in the discussion yourself, Mr. Cvetic. You already explained to us things concerning the KLA and so on. Can we move to the following page, please.
