The minutes say the following: He also stated that he is not receiving appropriate information of the state security sector concerning the activities of Siptar terrorists. Was this rightly recorded in the minutes that this is what you said?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received some information, but these were not timely information, nor were they complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, at this meeting we will see on page 3 what was stated by General-Major Sreten Lukic, and then on page 4 we can see that if we have a problem with the exchange of information between state security sector and public security sector please inform me so that we can overcome that problem?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably he did say this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this was included in the minutes, although I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not want to be misunderstood here. The information, at least when it comes to SUP Kosovska Mitrovica, did not -- which were coming from the state security sector, were not timely, nor complete. They sent information first of all to the centre of the state security sector, the centre of the state security sector would forward the information to the leader of the state security sector for Kosovo and Metohija, and then it would be forwarded on. So it was up to them to decide which information they would forward and which they wouldn't. So the selection of the information was done by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on page 3, could you please comment on following: Can you remember that Colonel Mijatovic was talking about forwarding OSCE Mission and Verification Mission about any movement of the forces two days ahead, and he requested from SUP chiefs it to carry out all the relevant tasks and report about this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is what indeed happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you reported according to this instruction as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the Exhibit P1043.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, these are the minutes of the meeting at the ministry staff on the 21st of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Actually, while we were on the first page, we can see that the meeting was attending by the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And also General-Colonel Stevanovic; the head of the office as well, Danilo Pantovic; and other persons listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here you can see this part: "Today General Stevanovic will convey to you my instructions concerning the activities in the newly arisen situation." Can you see this portion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, did General Stevanovic convey to you present at the meeting the instructions of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because this is what is recorded in these minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is also stated here that the minister informed you he had to leave before General Stevanovic took over chairing of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that the minister left earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see that it is written here that the minister with General Lukic, Ilic, and Pantovic, left the meeting at 11.30 in order to attend a meeting in Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is recorded here, most probably it happened, but I can't remember them leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And we can see that after this you were the first to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the Exhibit P764.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, now we will see the minutes of the staff meeting on the 4th of April, 1999. So the agenda of these meetings were the previous tasks and achieved results and then forthcoming tasks and other matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You attended this meeting, did you not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that all chiefs of SUPs took part in the discussion on the first item of the agenda?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the commanders as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you invited by the staff leader to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So everybody who attended the meeting received an invitation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Either an invitation in writing or we were invited by phone. Usually we were invited by phone, but for the meeting on the 16th of April, we received a dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that at this meeting the commanders also reported under the first item of the agenda?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On this page we can see that, first of all, it was Bosko Petric, then Ljubinko Cvetic, and then another person took part in the discussion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was in line with the seating arrangement during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We can see here that detachment commanders also took part in the discussion of the 35th, 36th, and 37th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the discussion of the commander of the 35th, 37th, and 23rd Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We have the two commanders of the 21st and 22nd PJP Detachments, and then Zeljko Trajkovic who was an SAJ commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: He was in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here it says Miodrag Jankovic, JSO commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We were told here that this is actually Milorad Ulemek, the JSO commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During 1998 and 1999, I saw Mr. Ulemek in Kosovo. He commanded the JSO unit. Milorad Lukovic Ulemek, aka Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is addressing the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But here it says Milorad Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It was established that it was a topographical error. It says here units of the VJ is cooperating with them and is well equipped. However, it is comprised of members of the reserve force that cannot be relied upon in the subsequent operations and hence it is suggested that they be replaced. You probably don't recall that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember such issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 2 the same page, the following tasks issued by Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's turn the page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At page 4 we see that Obrad Stevanovic, assistant minister, took the floor.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: If Obrad Stevanovic were a PJP commander, would all these persons be reporting rather than he himself reporting as the commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these persons reported on the situation in their units and engagement of the units in their areas. This is how the briefing of the commanders of PJP units should be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But if he was the commander, I guess his commanders would not brief him at the staff meeting. It would rather be dealt with at a PJP command meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a question of method of that commander's work. Whether he wanted to have a separate meeting with his commanders, which he did - he did have separate meetings with them - but also at the staff meeting, the PJP commanders briefed on the situation in their units and the tasks they were performing in their areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As assistant minister he can convene a meeting following the minister's order which would include the PJP commanders, but first of all, let me ask you, where was the PJP command in Pristina in 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The PJP command in Pristina was in the building of the Pristina Secretariat until the building was bombed on the 29th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Of the 124th Intervention Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, where the MUP staff command was, and it encompassed all PJP units as its manoeuvre units in the area of Kosovo-Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as to avoid any misunderstandings, some people called the MUP staff in Pristina also the PJP command and they also -- some of them also called it PJP headquarters, but the real name of it was the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see here just below the agenda that the meeting was attended by the chiefs of all SUPs, commanders of PJP detachments, the SAJ commander, and the JSO commander of the RDB?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that only the minister could decide that the JSO be sent to Kosova-Metohija to assist?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All police engagement is decided on by the minister in both the public and state security sectors. I did not have access to the documents of the state security service; therefore, I don't know whether the chief of that sector was authorised by the minister to use the JSO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit P1039.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, for the transcript, could you please tell us the first and last names of the persons for whom you know were commanders of the JSO in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Milorad Lukovic Ulemek, aka Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This document was shown to you, Mr. Cvetic, earlier. Did you ever, as the chief of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, did you ever draw up a plan for an offensive anti-terrorist operation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the chief of the Secretariat?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the date of the 9th of April, you have no knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So as not to go through all of the documents - and you have seen them all - can I ask you to tell me whether I'm right about the documents concerning orders. First of all, did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see in the document, Actions or operations in the area of Cicavica. Yes, that was planned on the 9th of April to be conducted in the subsequent two or three days. They probably were, but the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP did not draw up plans to carry out such operations. Those plans were drawn up at the MUP staff following the chain of command of the police and the army, and then it was harmonised at the level of the Joint Command. That plan was forwarded to those who commanded the units in the field, or rather, that order was sent -- that document was sent either as an order or a decision. I explained what each of these contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were shown some orders here. Am I right in saying that you saw those orders for the first time in the course of the proofing by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which orders? That depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The ones that were shown to you, for example, to break up the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers should not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask that someone warn the speakers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because of the speed at which you're speaking and your overlapping, we have not been able to record the last two things. Now, you had a lot to say very quickly, Mr. Djurdjic. Is there any summary of that you want to record?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In keeping with your order, Your Honour, I'm trying to enable this witness to leave The Hague today. Therefore, I guess I'm being a bit hasty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's go a document at a time. The 15th of April document, you did not see that while you were in Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please tell me whether, at the time, you were familiar with the documents I'm about to show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit 972.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received it as the chief of the Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then document 971, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I saw this document for the first time during my testimony between the 4th and the 9th of December, 2006, before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1040. P972. It should be the decision on the break-up of the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Donja Drenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I've already said --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. I apologise. P1040 then. It should be the break-up of Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Bajgora 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please see the next page of it. I see here that the date is the 4th of May. At that time, I was not in the territory of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP or in Kosovo for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think this should be the 15th of April. I think that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see the first page, please, in the heading. At least my hard copy has that date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On my copy it says the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You are not familiar with this one?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have P969.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While waiting for it, Mr. Cvetic, did it strike you that under item 2 there's always a task or tasks issued to the Pristina Corps. Did you notice that observing these documents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have to explain this. The contents of an order and the methodology of its drafting is as follows: Each order has the first item as information on the enemy. Before that, we should have a geographical, topographical data, and additional information in that regard. The seconds item is the tasks of our forces, i.e., the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If this was the Joint Command, wouldn't it be logical to expect to have here the tasks of both the MUP and the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a matter of the Joint Command, whether they wanted to have that separately or whether they wanted to have that under the category of the Pristina Corps tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you notice in item 4 that the Joint Command always stated that they decided to support the MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was standard language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If something was joint, why would then they support it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had to support each other mutually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But why would the Pristina Corps support the MUP?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A, your pace. B, how can this witness tell you why the Joint Command wanted to do certain things? He can tell you why he might have wanted to do certain things, but he is not entirely the Joint Command, is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I was carried away because the witness was explaining the decisions, but I wanted to show him something else. Let's cease this line of questioning. Could we please have D104.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We shall see an order for the defeat and destruction of Siptar terrorist forces in the region of Malo Kosovo is that correct, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this was issued by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, you could see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This was a regular methodology whereby the tasks of the army and the MUP in the region of the Joint Command were coordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the Exhibit D115. I apologise, D105.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is the amendment of the decision that we saw a short while ago.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the area of Malo Kosovo and previously we spoke about Donja Drenica as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no. Do you want us to bring up the last document, if you forgot what it was all about? But please recall this number, the number that you can see here, 455-56/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see the document D104.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you can see the number here, so the previous document was a supplement or an amendment of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now again see D105, and can we please have the last page of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is an order, whereas the other one said amendment to the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you could see according to the questions 455-56 and then dash 56/1 so this was an amendment of this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the number under which they were recorded, but the right title should be amendment of the order of the item 4 of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, possibly somebody made a mistake, but you can see now who compiled this amendment to the decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says commander Major-General Vladimir Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So he amended the decision that was previously signed by the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he amended the order that was made by the Joint Command. He actually amended item 4 of that order, and item 4 considers the decision. What he amended here most probably regards the forces of the Pristina Corps, but I couldn't comment on it, really, without seeing this entire amendment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cvetic, all the decisions and orders that you saw, do all of them refer solely to the anti-terrorist activities against the forces of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not against the KLA, but it was simply to destroy and defeat the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. In the year of 1999, did you ever see any order to persecute civilians or to tolerate murders of Albanian population, the burning of their houses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such order, but these things did occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Also in your territory?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what did you do about this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in our territory we found some 90 bodies. The SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica secured this area, informed an investigative judge and state Prosecutor. They came and made a crime scene investigation, compiled the relevant documentation. They submitted a criminal report against an unknown perpetrator, and SUP undertook relevant measures in order to find this unknown perpetrator. So while I was in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica there were some 90 incidents. Against perpetrators of thefts or robberies or looting; or particularly against people who took away cars, vehicles and technical appliances, we filed criminal reports to the relevant court in Kosovska Mitrovica. I can't remember exactly how many such criminal reports were filed, but I believe between 25 and 30 for that reason and during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Cvetic, for answering my questions. Thank you, Your Honours, with this I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Well done. We will now have the second break and that will then allow Mr. Stamp to re-examine at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would mention, Mr. Stamp, that unfortunately, I was delayed on another matter. We can sit a little later, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That, I don't think, will be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said just now that: "In our territory we found some 90 bodies." Where did you find these 90 bodies?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of the Secretariat of Kosovska Mitrovica which means in the territory of SUP of the town of Kosovska Mitrovica and other organisational units of the Secretariat. So there were 90 bodies in total until the 16th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. These 90 bodies weren't found in one location?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could that be made a little more clear, Mr. Stamp. Are you saying at 90 separate times a body was found, or that altogether 90 bodies were found, sometimes more than one body with another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Sometimes more than one body would be found in one single place, but we did not find all the 90 bodies in one place. Sometimes we would find two, three, four, or five in one single location. Sometimes only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, you also said that in the afternoon of the 5th of April, you received some -- you received a phone call from Mr. Lukic in which he told you, among other things, to prevent the departure of civilians from their place of residence. Do you know what was occurring on the ground in the territory at that time which required Mr. Lukic to order the PJP commanders or to order you to take these measures?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, civilians were leaving their places of residence, so they were leaving the places in which they lived. And they were leaving in the direction of Macedonia, Albania, Montenegro, and also the central territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you recall if General Lukic followed up these instructions with a written dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not receive any such dispatch. I simply received this order via phone at 4.30 p.m. on 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the document 65 ter number 04147. And I should indicate, as I'm reminded, that this is P1048.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, or tell us whether or not this document was sent in furtherance of that oral order you received from General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it follows from these documents, one could draw such a conclusion from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. You told us in respect to another issue that the plans, the plans for combat activity or anti-terrorist actions, were drawn up at the MUP staff following the chain of command, by the police and the army and it that it was harmonised at the level of the Joint Command. I think you also told us earlier that the actual drafting of the plan was done by Pristina Corps staff. And you also said that the plan was forwarded to those who commanded the units in the field. Can you tell us how were these plans transmitted to these units? Let's start with the police units, do you know how the plans were transmitted to the police units in the field?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leader of the MUP staff in Pristina would invite to meetings the PJP commanders and they would be handed the plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the VJ units in the field, do you know how those were transmitted to them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I can only assume. And my assumption is that they were transmitted through the relevant chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cvetic. Your Honours, I have nothing further in re-examination, I please you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I refer you to your evidence earlier where you said that I remember that members of the Siptar ethnic community did not carry personal identification documents, I know that they did not carry IDs. Now is it that the Siptar did not carry personal IDs in certain areas or is it that they didn't carry IDs throughout the entire Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They did have personal identification documents, some of them did not have any. But what I said was that they did -- most of them didn't carry them with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I see. Now, did you see active combat against terrorists in Kosovska Mitrovica at all?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to know, Mr. Cvetic, that that concludes the questioning for you. It's been a long process. The Chamber would like to thank you for once again coming to The Hague and assisting us and for the concentration and attention that you've shown over five days here. You may, of course, now return to your normal activities. We thank you for all that you have done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any matter that needs to be discussed for the evidence next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we should discuss some of the matters that have been occupying my mind and my time in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.
